The results which were calculated with the SOFiSTiK programs are stored in the database. The task of the program MAXIMA is the determination of extreme values of the internal forces, stresses, displacements, support reactions and results of result sets.
 Different methods according to the partial safety concepts of the Eurocode and international design codes and according to the conventional method without partial safety factors can be used to determine the maximum values. Here MAXIMA finds the most unfavourable action effect and applies the combination factors automatically.
 To achieve this, the superposition is done in two steps. In the inner step MAXIMA finds the extreme value from different load cases of the action effect and in a second outer process the action effects are combined.
 The load cases to be superimposed may be defined unconditionally (e.g. dead load) or condi- tionally (e.g. live load). In a conditional superposition each load case is only applied if it has an unfavourable contribution. The definition of loads which exclude each other (alternate loads) or of loads with changing sign is also possible.
 The load cases which are used for the superposition can be combined through arbitrary com- binations of the calculated load cases. This occurs via the definition of subsequent load cases, which leads to an absolute superposition with the previous load cases. Each load case may be multiplied with a scaling factor, so that normalised loads can be used during the static analysis.
 The loads of non-linearly calculated load cases have to be include already the correspond- ing combination coefficients and safeties. A superposition with action effects (record ACT) is therefore not implemented. However, it is possible to make an alternative selection via the load cases only (record LC). Load cases which have been analysed non-linearly can only be superimposed as individual alternate load cases (TYPE AG1) with the factor 1.
 The results are printed and stored in the database for later design or visualisation purposes. The extent of the output can mainly be controlled by the user. It is recommended to print only the decisive or manually selected parts of the superposition.

Load cases which have been analysed non-linearly can only be superimposed as individual alternate load cases (TYPE AG1) with the factor 1.. The results are printed and stored in the database for later design or visualisation purposes. The extent of the output can mainly be controlled by the user. It is recommended to print only the decisive or manually selected parts of the superposition..
 The user should check the superposition by investigating random samples! With the input of LOAD and FACT in record ECHO all the defined and determined factors and the used load cases are output for every individual superposition value. Only the relevant superposition values are printed with all involved factors, if ECHO CHCK is input.

The superposition rule is determined via the definition of the design code in program AQUA (record NORM) or for the interactive input with SSD or SOFiPLUS at the beginning. MAXIMA then automatically uses the design code which is available in the database. The combination rules of the design codes as well as the National Annexes of the EN 1990 are different. For example, the EN 1990 with its National Annexes provides action combinations with safety and combination coefficients. In contrast, old standards such as DIN 1045 (1988) only combine load cases.
 The actions are already defined before the input of the loads in program SOFiLOAD or with the Action Manager in SSD. The corresponding load cases have to be allocated to the actions. The action can be only modified temporarily in MAXIMA. The superposition is done with partial safety factors and combination coefficients only for actions defined by arbitrary load cases. These load cases or combinations of them will be superimposed to define an action effect.
 A superposition contains all action effects which are defined by a combination rule with the record COMB.
 The most unfavourable variable action is designated as the leading variable action. MAXIMA selects the most unfavourable one and considers it according to the chosen combination rule. When using the explicit defined combination with action groups the determination of three leading variable actions is possible.
 The leading variable actions are marked with a * at sumQ1/sumQ2/sumQ3 (sum of the loads leading variable action) in the output with ECHO FACT FULL. This variable action which has the largest difference between sumL (sum of the loads leading variable action) and sumQI (sum of the loads acting variable) is used as leading variable action! The remaining variable actions are multiplied with the combination coefficient for the accompanying variable action in dependence on the combination rule.
 The default equations 2.1 till 2.7 correspond to the combinations which are given in the EN 1990 (except for equation 6.10a and 6.10b) and in the DIN 1055-100 / DIN-Fachberichte. For the special equations 6.10a and 6.10b of the EN 1990 and their use variants in the National Annexes it is recommended to use the explicit defined combinations.

The default equations 2.1 till 2.7 correspond to the combinations which are given in the EN 1990 (except for equation 6.10a and 6.10b) and in the DIN 1055-100 / DIN-Fachberichte. For the special equations 6.10a and 6.10b of the EN 1990 and their use variants in the National Annexes it is recommended to use the explicit defined combinations..
 For design codes, which are used other equations for the combinations e.g. BS 8110, BS 5400, Australian Standard, Indian Standard, US Standards, it is recommeded to use the explicit defined combination.
 If superposition defaults are available in the INI file for the selected design code, these defaults are used then in MAXIMA without input for COMB, ACT, ADD, LC and SUPP or in the SSD tasks Combination Rules and Superpositioning for Combination Rules. Precondition for this is the usage of the default actions of the record ACT (SOFiLOAD) or of the Loadcase Manager.
 You can find further explanations and examples for different design codes in our Online Help -> Tutorials
 https://www.sofistik.de/documentation/2025/en/tutorials/superpositions/superposition.html
 The number of processable load cases is limited to 999999. Upon request, the user can re- peatedly overwrite previously stored load cases or can recombine the load cases from different databases with DBINFO or DBMERG.
 The results can be stored under a new load case number. Possible available results of former calculations are deleted, unless, something else is requested with the input CTRL DELE.
 The superposition is made separately for each node and for each element or beam or design element section in the database.
 The superposition takes place for all nodes or elements even when not all of them have been selected. However, only the results for the selected nodes or elements are printed out. For special cases it is possible to make a selective superposition with the input SUPP OPT S.
 When the values to be superimposed are close to zero, then some problems arise for the imposed loads, in the calculation of the corresponding internal forces. This is handled by the program MAXIMA in the following manner: If the actual absolute value is less than 10E-6 of the maximum value of all load cases encountered, then the imposed load cases do not participate in the superposition.

When the values to be superimposed are close to zero, then some problems arise for the imposed loads, in the calculation of the corresponding internal forces. This is handled by the program MAXIMA in the following manner: If the actual absolute value is less than 10E-6 of the maximum value of all load cases encountered, then the imposed load cases do not participate in the superposition..
 If however the derivation of the quantity being superimposed is known, e.g. the shear force in the case of a superimposed bending moment, then an imposed load case is used if the corresponding derivation is positive.

content: For a superposition of non-linearly analysed load cases an envelope is formed. Only load cases without factors are superimposed here and only one decisive load case is determined. The superposition of non-linearly analysed load cases is only permitted, if the load cases are defined via alternative groups (record LC type AG1) or if the calculation occurred with a linearised calculation according to OENORM. If using the literal NONL for EXTR in record COMB, the load cases are processed automatically with TYPE AG1. It is to be noted here, that no action (no record ACT) has to be entered in MAXIMA even if the defined design code prescribes actions for superpositions after linear calculations.

metadata.sections: 2.6 Superposition of Non-linearly Analysed Load Cases

content: For special projects it can be necessary to execute an intermediate superposition. The deter- mined result load cases of an intermediate superposition can be used then as initial load cases for further combinations. For an intermediate superposition it is also possible here to assign the result load cases with COMB TYPE to an action which was defined before in SOFiLOAD.

When using load groups with ACT PART Q_1 till Q_99 it is possible to make intermediate superpositions internally within a MAXIMA run, e.g. for relevant traffic loads. The superposition with load groups is shown and described in the example file maxima_loadgroups.dat.
 For comparison the intermediate superposition with explicit MAXIMA definitions is shown in the example file maxima_intermediate-superposition.dat.

A hangar with two cranes has to be designed for seismic loading. In this case the standard load cases dead load (1 and 2) and three imposed load cases (4,5,6) are first available. The two independently moving cranes, each of them with 36 different load positions which are stored in the database with the load case numbers 101 to 172, are considered additionally.
 In a first step the extreme values of this loading are generated when the imposed loads and the crane loads are superimposed in three alternative groups. This requires, that one of the imposed load cases covers the full load.

The table summarizes the **record structure and input fields** for defining and printing **load case superpositions and combination rules** in SOFiSTiK’s MAXIMA workflow. It lists a set of records (e.g., `COMB`, `ACT`, `LC`, `SUPP`, etc.) and, for each record, the **items/parameters that must be provided**.

### Record overview (purpose in the overall procedure)
- **`HEAD` / `END`**: General wrapper records for the MAXIMA input (per SOFiSTiK manual “Basics”).
- **`COMB`**: Defines a **combination rule**. This is the place where the mathematical combination equations are set (e.g., examples like “EXTR DESI”). It typically specifies the combination “type” and metadata.
- **`ACT`** and **`LC`**: Identify the **actions** and the **load cases** to be combined. Actions/load cases are not arbitrarily created here; they must already exist from **SOFiLOAD**. They can be selected only and optionally modified in MAXIMA.  
  - If no modification of `ACT`/`LC` is needed (take them exactly as in SOFiLOAD), they can be omitted.
- **`SUPP`**: Defines the **actual superposition** (i.e., which `COMB` rule is applied and how the included parts are mapped, with indices for “from/to” and an increment).
- **`TRAC`**: Combination tracing for reporting how an element’s results are composed from contributing load cases. It requires a **separate MAXIMA run after superpositions** are computed.

### Field-level description from the table
The table has two columns: **Record** and **Items**.

#### `CTRL`
- `OPT`, `VAL`: Control options and values for the run/behavior.

#### `COMB`
- `NO`: Combination rule number/identifier.
- `EXTR`, `BASE`, `TYPE`: Parameters specifying the extraction/combination rule context and the type.
- `COMC`: Usually an additional classification/combination code.
- `TITL`: Title/label.

#### `ACT`
Action-related selection list (only required when actions need selection/possible modification inside MAXIMA):
- `TYPE`: Action type classification.
- `GAMU`, `GAMF`: Factors (e.g., partial safety/gamma-type parameters for action).
- `PSI0`, `PSI1`, `PSI2`, `PSIS`: Combination factors ψ (different levels/variants).
- `PART`: Part identifier.
- `SUP`: Indicates which superposition-related parameter set is used.
- `TITL`: Title.

#### `ADD`
Additional parameters for an action definition (or action adjunct factors):
- `TYPE`: Type classification.
- `FACU`, `FACE`: Factor parameters for ultimate/equivalent action influences.

#### `ADA`
- `TYPE`: Further action-related subtype (possibly for additional action groups).

#### `LC`
Load case selection list (required when load cases are included; may be omitted only in specific “standard combination” cases where actions/load cases are taken without input):
- `NO`: Load case number/identifier.
- `TYPE`: Load case type classification.
- `FACT`: Load case factor applied in the superposition.

#### `SUPP`
Superposition definition tying rule + mapping:
- `COMB`: Links to the chosen combination rule number.
- `EXTR`: Extraction mode/setting.
- `ETYP`: Element type / entity type.
- `TYPE`: Superposition/type classification.
- `FROM`, `TO`: Range defining which items (often load cases or element indices) are covered.
- `INC`: Increment step for the range.

#### `SUM`
- `COMB`, `LC`, `TITI` (shown as `TITI L` in the image), `TITL`: Aggregation/mapping fields connecting combination, load cases, and titles/labels.

#### `EXPO`
- `OPT`: Option controlling exponentiation/exposure-like output behavior.
- `TO`: Target parameter/endpoint.
- `PASS`: Pass/phase control for processing.

#### `ECHO`
- `OPT`, `VAL`: Echo/debug/control settings.

#### `TRAC`
Combination tracing setup (must be run separately after superpositions):
- `LC`: Load case for tracing.
- `ETYP`: Element type.
- `ELEM`: Element identification/class.
- `X`: Index (often section/node/position index).
- `SELE`: Selection mode.
- `OPT`: Options for tracing output.
- `CSAV`: Save/selection parameter.

### Workflow implication (how these records work together)
The table’s record set supports a **two-stage process**:
1. Define **combination rules** (`COMB`) and define or select **actions** (`ACT`/`ADD`/`ADA`) and **load cases** (`LC`) as needed, then create **superpositions** (`SUPP`).
2. Optionally define **tracing** (`TRAC`) in a **separate MAXIMA run** to print the contributing load cases for specific elements after `SUPP` exists.

Overall, the table is effectively a **schema** for MAXIMA input: it enumerates every record and the exact parameter fields required to build combination definitions, apply them to superpositions, and optionally trace their load case contributions.

Each row represents one **combination (COMB record)** selected by an identifier and characterized by its design-code-driven superposition type, load-case base references, and the set of result load cases generated.

**Key fields and meanings**

- **COMB / Item Description / NO (Combination number)**: An integer **1–999** identifying the preset combination. **NO=100 and above** are reserved for combinations that are preset from an INI configuration file. This value is central for uniquely referencing a rule.

- **EXTR (Kind of superposition)**: Encodes the **combination superposition concept** based on the active design code. The table supports multiple standardized combination categories, including:
  - **DESI**: design fundamental combination  
  - **ACCI**: design accidental combination (with leading variable action, denoted as ψ1,1*Qk,1)  
  - **EARQ**: design seismic combination  
  - **PERM**: serviceability permanent combination  
  - **RARE**: serviceability characteristic (rare) combination  
  - **FREQ**: serviceability frequent combination  
  - **NONF**: serviceability infrequent combination  
  - Simplified variants: **DESI-V, ACCI-V, RARE-V**  
  - **STAN**: standard combination (no partial safety factors and no combination coefficients)  
  - **NONL**: combination of non-linear calculated load cases  
  - **EXPL**: explicit defined combination (requires additional records to define participating actions/load cases)

- **BASE (Base load case number)**: A number that establishes the **reference base** for load cases used by the rule. It must be a **multiple of 100**, with a **minimum of 100**, and an upper limit up to **999900**. The table notes that BASE usage is further described elsewhere (e.g., “see description in record SUPP”). Units are effectively “Default −1 LT * − *” (as shown), indicating BASE is a constrained numeric parameter.

- **TYPE (Type of result load cases)**: Maps the combination rule to which **result load case category** it produces or applies. The table distinguishes:
  - **H**: primary loads  
  - **HZ**: primary and additional loads  
  - **NONE**: no assignment to any type for EC5/DIN 1052-2004  
  It also lists time-term result grouping options (for load combinations such as permanent/accidental):
  - **LT** long term, **MT** middle term, **ST** short term, **VT** very short term for accidental fire context
  - **FIRE**: fire combination or combination type tied to an already existing action (defined via record **ACT**)

- **LT (Item Description)**: Appears as a companion/type selector to TYPE, listing the valid result-case groupings and defaults (values include DESI, ACCI, EARQ, PERM, RARE, FREQ, NONF, STAN, plus LT/MT/ST/VT/FIRE-like groupings). It essentially enumerates the allowed long-term/term-based interpretation labels.

- **COMC (Copying of combinations)**: A mechanism that creates a **new combination rule** by copying an existing one and allowing modifications of **EXTR** and **BASE**. (This is structural metadata about how combination rules can be generated rather than a design parameter itself.)

- **TITL (Designation of the combination)**: A free-form label (example shown: “Lt32”) identifying the combination in outputs/UI.

**Behavioral/configuration rules (important for RAG context)**  
The table text describes how combinations are constructed: after selecting a combination rule with **COMB**, the program expects that the **actions (records ACT or ADD/ADA)** and their associated **load cases (records LC)** are provided **behind the corresponding COMB record**. The input table defines the configurable parameters for an **action (ACT)** in a structural load combination framework (used via SOFiLOAD/AQUA/MAXIMA). Each action has a short **TYPE** designation and is characterized by **partial safety factors** and **combination coefficients**, plus classification parameters that govern where the action participates in superposition and how multiple load cases inside the action are combined.

### Action identifiers and coefficients (top section)
- **TYPE**: Text designation of the action (e.g., preset literal), with default shown as `LIT4` (program-specific placeholder). This acts as the action “name” key in the configuration.
- **GAMU** (unitless): *Unfavourable partial safety factor*. Default marked as `*` (use system default).
- **GAMF** (unitless): *Favourable partial safety factor*. Default `*`.
- **PSI0**: Rare combination coefficient.
- **PSI1**: Frequent combination coefficient.
- **PSI2**: Quasi-permanent combination coefficient.
- **PS1S**: Infrequent combination coefficient (note: table lists `PS1S`; context text references `PSIS`, but both denote the infrequent coefficient family).
- **GAMA**: Partial safety factor for accidental actions.

These factors/coefficient values are stored per action and are later copied into load cases when actions are selected/instantiated; they may then be overridden per individual load case.

### Partitioning into superposition groups (PART)
- **PART**: Determines to which **action group** the action belongs in the superposition equations. The default is shown as `LIT` in the table and `*` indicates system default behavior.
  - **G** = permanent action
  - **P** = prestress
  - **Q** = variable action
  - **Q_1 … Q_99** = variable action load groups (supports staged combination without intermediate superpositions)
  - **A** = accidental action
  - **E** = seismic action

Context explains that for user-defined actions, **PART defaults to Q** unless explicitly provided, and all categories of a given action share the same PART (except that load groups Q_1…Q_99 may differ).

### Default superposition behavior inside the action (SUP)
- **SUP**: Controls the default treatment of multiple load cases within the action (i.e., how categories/load cases are considered during superposition). Default is `LIT` / `*`.
  - **PERM**: Permanent action with unique factor (sum then apply GAMU/GAMF).
  - **PERC**: Permanent action with individual factors per load case (a load case may use GAMU or GAMF separately).
  - **COND**: Conditional (only unfavourable cases).
  - **EXCL**: Mutually exclusive within category.
  - **EXEX**: Mutually exclusive within the entire action (across categories).
  - **UNSI**: Like COND but with special “unfavourable sign” behavior.
  - **USEX**: Like EXCL with unfavourable sign constraints.
  - **ALEX**: Permanent but exclusive within action (typically “always but exclusive” alternative-group behavior; only one load case considered even if favourable).

Additional context notes that these defaults can be overridden in MAXIMA for specific load cases, and provides extended literals (e.g., AG alternative groups, LC record behavior) to customize superposition/alternatives beyond the default SUP.

### Final field
- **TITLE**: Descriptive label for the action (default placeholder `LIT24`, with default `*`). This is for human readability rather than combination logic.

Overall, the table specifies a schema for defining actions with: (1) identification (TYPE, TITLE), (2) design-strength and combination parameters (GAMU/GAMF/PSI*/GAMA), and (3) rules governing how the action participates in global combination superposition (PART) and how its internal load cases/cultures of categories are reduced/selected (SUP).

The table defines the **set of predefined “actions” (action types)** used in the SOFiLOAD/AQUA/MAXIMA workflow, together with **their aliases for different loading categories**. It is essentially a legend mapping an action’s internal **Normal name** to how it is represented in the “Add.” and “Spec.” contexts, plus a short semantic description.

### Columns
- **Normal**: The primary action literal (e.g., `G_1^q`, `Q^q`, `A^x`).  
- **Add.**: The corresponding literal used when the action appears as an *additional* loading in the system (e.g., `ZG_1^g`, `ZQ^x`). These typically encode how the action is treated/inserted when added to load combinations.
- **Spec.**: The corresponding literal used for *special* handling in the system (e.g., `SG_1^q`, `SQ^x`).  
- **Remark**: Human-readable meaning of the action type.

### Rows and meaning (action taxonomy)
- `NONE` (remark: “for LC only: not assigned to an action”) indicates a placeholder/omission; it is not an actual action type assigned to a load case.
- **Permanent actions** (always applicable; marked by exponent `g`):
  - `G_?^g`:

This table should be indexed as a **mapping from action categories to ψ0/ψ1/ψ2 coefficients**. The input table defines parameters for a combination-related record (referenced in the context as **ADD**, used together with **COMB** and only under specific combination modes such as **COMB EXTR EXPL**). It has five columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.

## Column meanings
- **Item**: Short keyword that identifies the parameter field to be provided in the record.
- **Description**: Human-readable explanation of what the parameter represents and allowed values.
- **Unit**: Expected unit system or notation for the value (if applicable). For this table, the “unit” column often contains symbolic placeholders (e.g., `/LIT` variants) rather than physical units.
- **Default**: Default value indicator; in this table it is shown as **`!`**, meaning there is no implicit default and the user must supply these fields.

## Field: TYPE
- **Item**: `TYPE`
- **Meaning**: Selects the **designation of an action** or an **action group definition**. This drives which set of actions the ADD record will operate on.
- **Allowed group designators shown**:
  - `{G}`: all permanent actions
  - `{P}`: all actions due to prestress and creep
  - `{Q1}`, `{Q2}`, `{Q3}`: first/second/third leading variable actions
  - `{Q}`: all variable actions
- **Additional interpretation of `{Q}`**:
  - Without leading variable actions: `{QI} = all`
  - With leading variable actions: `{QI} = remaining variable actions`
- Other group shortcuts:
  - `{A}`: all accidental actions
  - `{E}`: all seismic actions
- **Unit**: `LIT4` (symbolic; indicates a literal type/format required by the system)
- **Default**: `!` (mandatory)

## Field: FACU
- **Item**: `FACU`
- **Meaning**: Unfavourable factor, literal, or expression. It can be:
  - a numeric factor (unfavourable),
  - a literal reference,
  - or a formula of the form `=factor*literal`.
- **Unit**: `—/LIT` (symbolic; indicates it is tied to a literal type rather than a physical unit)
- **Default**: `!` (mandatory)

## Field: FACF
- **Item**: `FACF`
- **Meaning**: Favourable factor, literal, or expression, similarly supporting:
  - literal references and
  - formulas of the form `=factor*literal`.
- **Unit**: `—/LIT`
- **Default**: `!` (mandatory)

## Contextual constraints (from provided additional text)
The **ADD** record is only usable with **COMB EXTR EXPL**. The table’s `TYPE`, `FACU`, and `FACF` parameters are part of defining how actions contribute during an explicit defined combination. Actions must be provided via `SOFiLOAD` record `ACT` to be available after calculation, and action-to-group assignment is governed by `PART` in record `ACT`. Importantly, after using an **action group**, a subsequent `LC` record is not allowed (since the program determines load cases itself), and assigning load cases to other categories via `ADD` is forbidden and will interrupt calculation with an error.

The input table contains a single row describing a parameter used in a structural “action” selection/superposition context. It has four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.

### Column meanings
- **Item**: Identifies the parameter name. In the provided row, the parameter is **TYPE**.
- **Description**: Explains what the parameter controls.
- **Unit**: The unit for the value of the parameter; for this row, there is none in the usual sense because **TYPE** is categorical.
- **Default**: Indicates the default value when the parameter is not explicitly provided; here it is shown as **“!”**, suggesting a required/flagged default or a placeholder indicating “no meaningful numeric default” (common in configuration templates).

### Row: TYPE
- **TYPE** is described as: *“Designation the action from the selected action group”*.
- The **Unit** column shows **LIT4** and the **Default** column shows **!**.
  - **LIT4** likely denotes a specific coding/identifier format (e.g., a literal or enumerated type reference) used by the system to interpret the **TYPE** value.
  - The **!** default implies that **TYPE** is not automatically determined; it must be explicitly specified, or the system triggers an error/required-field behavior if omitted.

### Semantics in context (from the provided surrounding text)
Within the broader command syntax (e.g., the use of records such as `ADD`, `ADA`, and the notion of **action groups**), the system determines which actions participate in calculations. **ADA** controls *which actions are selected* within an action group during superposition, and actions must be defined/loaded (e.g., via `SOFiLOAD record ACT`) so they are available in the database. In this workflow, **TYPE** serves as the selector/identifier that designates *which action* (from the already chosen action group) is targeted.

### RAG-friendly summary

content:
The provided table is a configuration/reference table for **load case selection and superposition parameters** used in structural analysis design checks. It standardizes how different **load actions** (e.g., permanent, conditional, alternating, follow-up) are referenced and combined through a set of coded fields, including load-case numbering, load-case type, and safety factor handling rules.

### Key components and meaning of the fields
1. **Load case number (LC)**
   - The table uses an **“LC” identifier** to specify which load case(s) are used.
   - Special meanings are defined:
     - **“0”**: use **all load cases** of the defined action.
     - **“-1”**: use **all load cases** of the defined **category**.
     - Otherwise, an explicit **positive/individual LC number** indicates the selected load case(s).

2. **Item / Description (context header column)**
   - The table includes an **item description** indicating how each record should be interpreted.
   - A notation like **“Item Description”** suggests that each row defines a specific combination rule or action/load-case behavior.

3. **TYPE — Type of load**
   - The **TYPE** field defines how the action behaves in the design combination framework. Codes include:
     - **G**: **Always (permanent)** load type.
     - **PERM**: permanent action (with “permanent” also described as **permanent with alternative handling** via other rules).
     - **SUP Q / COND**: **Conditional** load; only taken for the **unfavourable** side (with “Q” meaning the same as “COND”).
     - **SUP W / UNSI**: **Alternating** load case is used, with sign-sensitive behaviour: if it acts unfavourably (e.g., certain seismic cases), the combination accounts for the positive/negative direction.
     - **SUP F**: **Follow-up** load is added to the previous **main** load case, but only if the main load case is included during superposition.

4. **SUP PERC — Partial safety factor handling**
   - The table distinguishes between:
     - **SUP PERC “Always (permanent)”**: permanent loads use partial safety factors **action-wise** (i.e., consistent across the action).
     - **SUP PERC “from record ACT item”** (for permanent): for variable factors, partial safety factors may be applied **load-case-wise** based on the referenced “ACT item”.

5. **AG — Alternative load case groups (AG1 to AG99)**
   - The table defines **AG groups** as **permanent alternative load case groups**.
   - Rows may specify **AG1 (always)** up to **AG99 (always)**.
   - The table also indicates an operation: either the **initial load case is multiplied** or alternatively **default unit/alternative selection logic** applies (“Unit Default − * LT * …”), implying that AG groups provide multiple permanent alternatives within one action but remain **exclusive within one action**.

6. **LC combination / unit load case usage**
   - The note states that with the **LC field**, “any desired combinations” can be analysed or already-combined load cases may be defined for superposition.
   - It also explains that each load case can be reused for different load case types, enabling (under certain conditions) working with **unit load cases** in a static analysis.

### Overall purpose
This table functions as a **domain-specific coding scheme** for controlling how load cases are:
- selected (via LC with special values like 0 and -1),
- categorized by behaviour (via TYPE: permanent, conditional, alternating, follow-up),
- combined with appropriate **partial safety factors** (SUP PERC rules),
- and managed through alternative permanent groups (AG1–AG99).

It is designed to ensure consistent and auditable interpretation of structural loading combinations across design checks and superposition scenarios.

The table defines a configuration field for **load case selection/grouping and an associated scaling factor**, intended for structural load combinations (superposition). It has the columns:

- **Item**: identifies the parameter being configured (e.g., ALEX, FACT). In the excerpt, at least two items are shown: one describing the load case grouping selector and one defining a multiplier.
- **Description**: provides detailed semantics for the item, including allowed values, notation conventions, and constraints.
- **Unit**: indicates the physical unit of the parameter. For these configuration-style fields, it is shown as a symbolic unit (or blank), not a physical dimension.
- **Default**: gives the default value used when the parameter is not explicitly specified.

### Item / parameter: ALEX (from record ACT item SUP (= AG1))
The **Description** indicates that **ALEX** is derived from another record field: it is “**from record ACT item SUP (= AG1)**”. This ties the current configuration to a higher-level definition of **alternative load case groups** (AG*).

The table further enumerates possible values for the selector:

- **A1 … A99**: “Alternative load case group A1 … A99”.  
  - Each group is **exclusive within one action**, meaning that for a given action only one alternative group member should be chosen in the combination (avoiding simultaneous selection within the same action).
- **EXCL from record ACT item SUP**: an alias referencing the value directly from the ACT definition.
- **X1 … X99**: “Alternative load case group X1 … X99 with changing sign”.  
  - These represent load alternatives where the **sign may be inverted**, relevant when a “favourable/unfavourable” sense depends on whether the load acts positively or negatively (e.g., certain directional effects).
- **USEX from record ACT item SUP**: another alias directly referencing the ACT definition.
- **Default: see below**: indicates the actual default behavior is specified in a later part of the documentation.
- Constraint: “**For non-linear load cases only AG1 is permitted**.”  
  This means alternative group selection is restricted when nonlinear effects are present; only the initial/permitted baseline alternative group is allowed.

Context from the provided notes aligns with this: alternative load case groups **AG1…AG99** are permanent alternative groups; they can be used in superposition, and under certain circumstances load cases can be treated as “unit load cases” in static analysis when multiplied.

### Item / parameter: FACT
The **FACT** row defines **a numerical factor** applied to the corresponding internal forces:

- Meaning: “**Factor with which the corresponding internal force of the initial load case is multiplied**.”
- **Unit**: shown as “−/LIT” in the excerpt (i.e., a dimensionless ratio or a symbolic unit consistent with a scaling factor per load case type).
- **Default**: **1.0**, meaning no scaling is applied unless specified.

### Overall interpretation for RAG indexing
This table segment documents a **load combination programming interface**: you choose an **alternative load case group selector (AEX/A1…A99, X1…X99, with sign change options and ACT-based aliases)** with a default governed elsewhere and with a nonlinear-only restriction (AG1 only). Separately, you can scale the resulting internal forces from an “initial load case” via **FACT**, defaulting to 1.0.

 Among the load cases of an alternative load case group, only the one with the most detrimental effect is used for a superposition. In special cases it can be necessary to generate a combination of different superposition values in one result load case. This can be for example a foundation check, where the combination of the minimum vertical load and the maximum horizontal load is very important. The resultant shear force of plates can be also from interest and can be generated with the shear forces v-x and v-y. The user has the possibility to form a reasonable combination of superposition values by using a objective function.
 A objective function is generated with superposition values (described above at TYPE) and perhaps with factors or defined variables (LET or STO variables). An objective function for example for the resultant shear force of a plate reads as follows:
 SUPP COMB 1 EXTR mami ETYP quad TYPE 'SQR(VX**2+VY**2)' LC 101
 Using the objective function, then some rules are to be considered:
 • The superposition values are to be combined reasonably. Only the superposition values of one element type ETYP are to be defined.
 • The rules for CADINP are valid. An objective function should be input with quotation marks ’...’. Blanks are avoid.
 • The result load case number of a superposition with an objective function has to be input manually.
 The determination of an superposition result with an objective function runs exactly with a linear function. For a quadratic function it is to be noted that following relationship is valid
 ( + y)2 > 2 + y2
 If a factor which is defined either explicitly or with a variable is input, it is to be noted that the factor is used only for the weighting during processing of the objective function. This factor does not come in into the numerical value of the superposition result! As an use for that the determination of the boundary stresses is mentioned.
 The user is even responsible for the superposition with an objective function. The user should check the superposition here! With the input of LOAD and FACT in record ECHO all the defined and determined factors and the used load cases are output for every individual superposition value. Only the relevant superposition values are printed with all involved factors, if ECHO CHCK is input.

The user is even responsible for the superposition with an objective function. The user should check the superposition here! With the input of LOAD and FACT in record ECHO all the defined and determined factors and the used load cases are output for every individual superposition value. Only the relevant superposition values are printed with all involved factors, if ECHO CHCK is input..
 Possibilities of an input of an objective function are subsequently described here:
 SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP node TYPE 'PX+PY' LC 5101
 describes as objective function an addition of the support reactions PX and PY.
 The Definition of the variable STO#fact 2.5 and
 SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP node TYPE '#(fact,2.1)*PX+PY' LC 5101
 describe as objective function an addition of the support reactions PX and Py where PX is
 used with a 2.5-times weighting. The input #(fact,2.1) has the effect that the CADINP variable is used with maximal two digits before and one digit behind the ., therefore with 2.5. If only #fact is input, then the value of the variable is rounded off on 3, because CADINP used so only integer values. It is also possible to input the factor 2.5 directly into the objective function:
 SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP node TYPE '2.5*PX+PY' LC 5101

Result sets are used for grouping and for common evaluation of results. They are defined in program SOFiMSHA with RSET. In MAXIMA it is possible to determine the relevant values for a result value. These are for example support reactions in several points and spring forces in different directions.
 For evaluation the literal RSET has to be input at ETYP, the respective ID of the single elements at TYPE and the respective ID of the set (header in SOFiMSHA) at FROM. The ID of the set (header in SOFiMSHA) and the respective single elements can be a number or a literal. It is to be considered that an ID, which is defined as a number, can be input with or without apostrophes both in the program SOFiMSHA and in MAXIMA. The input has to be identical in both programs.
 The results sets have to be input separately. Several result sets can be also defined as a CADINP loop. An input for TO is not allowed.
 The result load case number of a superposition with a results set has to be input manually. It should be noted here, that different result load case numbers have to be defined for different RSET.
 Example: Definition of a RSET for spring forces
 In the example which is shown below the ID of the set is the number 2 and it is input in MAXIMA at SUPP ... FROM. The IDs of the single sets are here ’PVER’ and ’PAXI’.
 PROG SOFIMSHA HEAD ... RSET ID '2' TITL 'Bearing type 2' RSET ID 'PAXI' NO 1002 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'longitudinal' RSET ID 'PVER' NO 1003 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'transverse' ... END
 PROG MAXIMA
 HEAD ECHO RSET FULL COMB ... ... SUPP COMB EXTR ETYP TYPE FROM LC TITL='Bearing type 2' 1 MAMI RSET 'PVER' '2' 2000

RSET ID '2' TITL 'Bearing type 2' RSET ID 'PAXI' NO 1002 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'longitudinal' RSET ID 'PVER' NO 1003 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'transverse' ... END. PROG MAXIMA. HEAD ECHO RSET FULL COMB ... ... SUPP COMB EXTR ETYP TYPE FROM LC TITL='Bearing type 2' 1 MAMI RSET 'PVER' '2' 2000.
 1 MAMI RSET 'PAXI' '2' 2010
 END
 Special Feature for Bearing Forces in Bridge Design
 The bearings of a superstructure are created with springs. Then results sets (RSET) are gener- ated for these springs in order to determine the relevant bearing values with the corresponding values of the other bearing axes after calaculation.
 If more results sets (RSET) exist with the same result values, only the ID of one RSET has to be input at FROM. Then the result values of all RSET are always superimposed and the corresponding other values of the result sets are saved in the same corresponing load cases.
 Example for the definition of the result sets (RSET) in SOFiMSHA:
 #define RSET
 RSET ID 'PX' SET SPRI ITEM P NO #start+0 TITL 'PX' RSET ID 'PY' SET SPRI ITEM P NO #start+1 TITL 'PY' RSET ID 'PZ' SET SPRI ITEM P NO #start+2 TITL 'PZ' #enddef
 let#start 200101 RSET ID 'L10L' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 10 left' #include RSET
 let#start 200101
 let#start 200107
 let#start 200107
 RSET ID 'L10R' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 10 right'
 #include RSET
 let#start 200201 RSET ID 'L20L' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 20 left' #include RSET
 let#start 200207
 RSET ID 'L20R' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 20 right'
 #include RSET
 Four result sets L10L, L10R, L20L and L20R are available with their respective result values PX,PY and PZ for the spring force.
 With the following MAXIMA definition these result values of all four result sets are superim- posed although only L10L is input at FROM.

Four result sets L10L, L10R, L20L and L20R are available with their respective result values PX,PY and PZ for the spring force.. With the following MAXIMA definition these result values of all four result sets are superim- posed although only L10L is input at FROM..
 SUPP
 ETYP
 TYPE
 LC
 EXTR=MAMI COMB=11
 FROM
 'RSET' 'PX' 81001 'L10L' 'RSET' 'PY' 81003 'L10R' 'RSET' 'PZ' 81005 'L10R'

With FROM, TO and INC it is possible to control the output of structural elements, groups or individual elements. This is useful for instance, if superposition results should be checked with random samples for all the used load cases and factors (ECHO LOAD,FACT). In a first internal calculation MAXIMA determines the superposition results of all elements. In a second calculation only the selected elements are considered. Only the selected elements are printed then.
 Selection of structural elements:
 Results of elements can be also printed in dependence on the selected structural element. In this case the literals SLN or SAR have to be choosen at FROM. The number of the structural element can then be defined at TO. An input at INC has here no effect. A selection of structural areas is not possible for nodal results. A selection of structural lines is not possible for results of design elements.
 Group selection:
 Results of elements can be also printed groupwise. In this case the literal GRP has to be choosen at FROM. The group number or the name of a secondary group can then be defined at TO. An input at INC has here no effect.
 A group selection is not possible for nodal results. If the internal forces and moments in the nodes of plane and volume elements (ETYP QNOD, BNOD) should be printed groupwise, the group number has to be defined at SELE.
 Element selection:
 If an element selection is desired, then the element or node numbers can be input at FROM and TO whereat INC defines the increment. In the case of an input of only an element or node number at FROM only the superpositon result of this number is printed.
 Selection of a specific tower for the storey results:
 For the storey results it is possible to select only a specific tower for the output of the results with FROM ’TOWR’ and the corresponding ID.
 Without an input at FROM, TO and INC and with a corresponding ECHO option (e.g. ECHO FACT, ECHO QUAD, ECHO BEAM) the results for all elements or nodes are printed which are available.

 Using record SUM, sums of results from individual load cases with manually defined factors can be determined. Therefore, the use of record SUM is only allowed for standard com- binations COMB EXTR STAN and related initial load cases which have to be defined as permanent. All defined initial load cases are always taken into account for the determination of the sum, even if they have a favourable effect.
 Example:
 COMB 1 EXTR STAN TYPE DESI LC 1 TYPE PERM FACT 1.35 LC 2 TYPE PERM FACT 1.5 LC 4 TYPE PERM FACT 1.5 LC 8 TYPE PERM FACT 1.05
 The superposition values are determined automatically for the respective system.
 The combination rule is automatically deleted after calculation of the superposition results. Only the superposition results are stored in the database. Therefore, it is not possible to execute superpositions with record SUPP simultaneously with record SUM for such a special combination.
 For the designation TITL 32 characters are available. The input designation can have, however, only 28 characters, because the program uses automatically 4 characters for an information about the superposition at the beginning of the designation.
 Definition of the load lase number:
 Only one resulting load case can be defined at item LC for a standard combination with de- termination of sums. All superposition results are stored in this load case. It is not allowed to define a base load case number BASE in record COMB for the standard combination (only BASE 0 is possible).
 Output extent:
 In addition to the default TABU YES in record ECHO, the extended output can be additionally selected with ECHO FULL FULL or ECHO LOAD,FACT. A selection of individual elements or the printout of the relevant values is not possible. For this purpose, the output of lists is recommended in the Result Viewer.

The input table defines the **output option (record field)** used to control what kind of information is printed during a **load case combination / superposition** procedure. It is organized as a matrix with columns **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.

### Columns
- **Item (OPT)**: Identifies the controllable parameter that selects the output mode.
- **Description**: Provides the allowed literal values for **OPT** and explains what each mode outputs.
- **Unit**: Shown as a placeholder for the list-literal type; for this table it references **LIT** (literal).

### Allowed OPT values and their meanings
The **Description** cell lists the following literals (each mapped to a specific print behavior):

1. **NO — No printed output**

2. **TABS — General tables of the combinations and generated load cases**

3. **CHCK — Output of the decisive point of superposition**

8. **BOUND / BOUN — Single values of boundary elements / Support sums of boundary elements**

9. **BEAM — Beam elements**

11. **TRUS — Truss elements**

12. **CABL — Cable elements**

14. **CFM — Forces of kinematic constraints**

15. **QUAD — Plane elements**

16. **QNOD — Plane elements, values in nodes**

17. **BRIC — Solid elements**

18. **BNOD — Solid elements, values in nodes**

19. **QBED — Bedding values**

20. **BSEC — Beam element sections**

21. **RSET — Result sets**

### Additional context embedded in the source text
The surrounding notes (preceding the table) explain that the OPT-like output controls are typically part of **ECHO**-style records, where:
- “FULL” is extensive and may increase compute time and file size.
- “LOAD”/“FACT” provide checks of participating load cases and their coefficients.

### Table description: “ECHO / SUPP output and load case combination control” (continuation)

This table segment documents an **output control interface** for generating and printing **load case combinations and superposition results**. It explains how different **ECHO** (echo/print) options influence what is written to the output listing (and, in some cases, to the database), and how this interacts with the **record SUPP** (superposition). The table is presented in a key–value style where short option keywords determine the output extent and content.

#### Options and their meaning
- **See also: SUPP**  
  Indicates that this output control table is closely related to the `SUPP` record, which defines superpositions.

- **ECHO** (group header / controlling record)  
  The `ECHO` record selects which intermediate values, combination rules, and decisive points are printed.

- **VAL – “Value of output option”**  
  A column/section describing the meaning of the option value used by the program.

- **LT**  
  Shown as an option value marker; appears in the same “keyword-to-result” grouping, indicating a threshold/limit-style behavior in the output logic (exact semantics depend on the full program context).

- **“*”**  
  Used as a wildcard-like symbol in the option-value column, implying “all” or “any” depending on the record context.

- **NO – “No printed output”**  
  Selecting `NO` suppresses output for the respective echo option.

- **YES – “Regular output”**  
  Selecting `YES` enables the standard amount of output for that option.

- **P – “Output of forces or stresses”**  
  Enables printing of force/stress-related results (i.e., results typically relevant to structural response).

#### How output extent is controlled (behavioral rules)
The provided text specifies multiple important behaviors:

1. **Load case combinations and factors:**  
   The “first two tables” (for selected load cases) include the **load case factors**, plus defined **GAMMA** and **PSI** values, and the **generated load cases**.  
   With **ECHO TABS YES** (default), only those combinations actually used for superpositions are printed.  
   With **ECHO TABS FULL**, all combinations available in the database are printed.

2. **When no SUPP definitions exist:**  
   If only combination rules are defined (in MAXIMA input) and there are **no superposition definitions** (i.e., no record `SUPP`), then explicit **ECHO TABS FULL** can be used to print combination-rule output and the table “Load case selection and actions.” Superposition results are printed only if `ECHO` is provided explicitly.

3. **Placement of ECHO relative to SUPP:**  
   An explicit `ECHO` input must be placed **before the record `SUPP`** to control output per superposition. If multiple `ECHO` records appear consecutively, the record name `ECHO` must be repeated for each record to avoid confusion.

4. **Detailed factors output:**  
   - **ECHO FACT FULL** prints all involved **GAMMA/PSI** values and derived factors in detail.  
   - **ECHO FACT YES** prints only factors **unequal to zero**.  
   Default for `FACT` is **FULL**. There is an explicit recommendation to validate superposition results using random samples.

5. **Decisive-point printing:**  
   - **ECHO CHCK** prints only the decisive point after superposition (similar in role to `ECHO LOAD` and `ECHO FACT`).  
   - When an element/node selection is applied to `SUPP` using `SUPP FROM TO INC` together with `ECHO CHCK`, only relevant selected values are printed.

6. **Result-set interaction:**  
   If **ECHO CHCK** is used, it has **no influence on Result Sets**, and **ECHO RSET YES is set**.

7. **Database saving of factors:**  
   - **ECHO CHCK CSAV** stores combination factors in the database as a combination rule, assigning the resulting load case numbers (must be **1 to 999** due to `COMB` limits).

8. **Special/extended outputs:**  
   - **ECHO BSEC FULL** prints beam section results, which normally should not be printed due to program behavior in `SOFiMSHA`.

9. **Summary of combinations:**  
   - **ECHO SUM YES** requests an overview of determined load case combinations.

#### Practical hint included
For large systems with many elements, the text recommends extensive outputs only for **a selected element**, using `ECHO CHCK` or selecting elements in `SUPP` with `FROM` and then using echo options accordingly. Printing extensive output for all elements can increase computation time and create a very large PLB file.

The table describes the input parameters for the **MAXiMA command TRAC**, which traces how a **resulting (superposed) load case** was generated from its **input load cases** and their **factors**.

## Overall purpose
You specify a *resulting load case number* and an *entity location/type* (element type, element/node identifier, and optionally coordinates or stress-point selection). TRAC then reads the originally used **SUPP** (superposition) and **COMB** (combination) information from the database, identifies all contributing **input load cases** that were combined to obtain the target result, and prints them with their factors. This is intended for investigating which input actions led to a critical load case on a specific model entity.

## Table fields

### 1) **LC**
- **Meaning:** The **resulting load case number** from a previous MAXiMA run that you want to trace.
- **Unit:** “–”
- **Default:** “!” (required / no default)

### 2) **ETYP** (element type)
- **Meaning:** The **type of the entity** for which the trace is requested.
- **Default:** LIT
- **Allowed values (with interpretation):**
  - **NODE**: Nodes
  - **SPAC**: Nodal accelerations and nodal velocities
  - **BOUN**: Boundary elements
  - **BOUS**: Sums of boundary elements
  - **BEAM**: Beams
  - **DSLN**: Design elements
  - **BSCT**: External beam sections (from program SIR)
  - **TRUS**: Trusses
  - **CABL**: Cables
  - **SPRI**: Springs
  - **CFM**: Kinematic constraints
  - **QUAD**: Plane elements
  - **QNOD**: Nodes of plane elements
  - **QBED**: Bedding of plane elements
  - **BRIC**: Volume elements
  - **BNOD**: Nodes of volume elements
  - **RSET**: Result set
  - **SLVL**: Storey results

### 3) **ELEM**
- **Meaning:** An **element or node number** (or an identifier of a result set), depending on ETYP.
- **Default:** “!”
- **Unit:** “–”
- **Notes:** For example, when ETYP refers to nodes/elements, ELEM identifies the specific target object.

### 4) **X**
- **Meaning:** Additional coordinate selector used for **BEAM elements** (beam axis position) or for design element selection (design element’s relevant x-position).
- **Unit:** **m**
- **Default:** “-”
- **Relevance:** Required when the target is a beam and you need a position along the beam.

### 5) **SELE**
- **Meaning:** Selection index whose meaning depends on ETYP:
  - For **BEAM and DSLN**: **cross section point** (e.g., stress point) within the section
  - For **QNOD and BNOD**: **group number** for the plane/volume element nodes
  - For **BOUN**: **node number** for the relevant boundary
- **Unit/Format:** shown as “–/Lit⁴” (as displayed in the table)
- **Default:** “-”
- **Notes:** Particularly important when tracing results that refer to cross-section stresses (SIG/TAU), where stress point selection is needed.

### 6) **OPT** (tracing options)
- **Meaning:** Controls the **depth** of tracing, i.e., whether TRAC resolves only the first level of input load cases or includes **intermediate superpositions**.
- **Default:** **IF**
- **Values shown in table:**
  - **I**: Trace intermediate superpositions  
- **Meaning of “IF” (implied by context):** stop earlier (first level / do not expand intermediate superpositions).

In summary, the table enumerates the required identifiers and selectors to pinpoint the target result location (via LC + ETYP + ELEM + optional X/SELE) and the option that controls how deeply TRAC expands the superposition chain.

### Table Description (TRAC command / CSAV output and subsequent transformation)

This table documents the purpose and usage workflow of the **TRAC** command in **MAXiMA** in the context of **superposition of load cases** and the optional **saving/transformation** of traced results into new load case combinations and load cases.

#### 1) What TRAC does
Using the command **TRAC**, a user can **trace a specific resulting Load Case** that was produced by a **MAXiMA superposition**. TRAC determines and prints the **input Load Cases** that contributed to the resulting load case, along with their **multiplication factors** as used by the superposition. This enables investigation of how a **critical load case on a particular element** was generated.

#### 2) Required input parameters (key selection fields)
The command requires:
- **LC**: the **number of the resulting Load Case** to be traced.
- **ETYP**: the **element type** where the result belongs (e.g., BEAM, QUAD, BRIC, BOUN).
- **ELEM**: the **element number**.
Additional, element-dependent parameters:
- For **BEAM**: **X position** must also be specified.
- For BEAM cross-section stress results (e.g., **SIG / TAU**): **SELE** must define the **stress point** (analogous to SUPP record behavior).
- For **QUAD/BRIC** when SELE is used for node-grouping: SELE may specify a **group number** for nodes (**QNOD/BNOD**).
- For **BOUN** (boundary elements): **node number** must be provided for the relevant boundary via **SELE**.

#### 3) Depth control via OPT
- **OPT** controls the **tracing depth**, i.e. whether TRAC resolves **intermediate superpositions** or stops at the **first level** of identified input load cases.

#### 4) SUPP/COMB retrieval and validation behavior
TRAC reads the corresponding **SUPP** and **COMB** information (used originally during the superposition) from the database, then retrieves the associated **input load cases** and factors.
- If the **result type is stored** in the database, TRAC can **validate** that the recomputed tracing result matches the stored result.
- If the result type is computed **on-the-fly** (not stored), validation is not possible. Examples include:
  - BEAM cross-section stresses at stress points
  - Von Mises stresses for QUAD elements

#### 5) Execution constraints / limitations
- Tracing must be performed in an **individual MAXiMA run**; it cannot be combined with standard superposition functionality.
- It is **not possible** to trace superpositions associated with **Tendon Stresses for Quad Elements**.

#### 6) Saving traced results using CSAV
The table explains that traced load case factors can be saved into a **new load case combination** by providing:
- **CSAV**: a **combination number** where the new combination is stored.

After saving, the user can generate new load cases using **SOFiLOAD**:
- In **SOFiLOAD**, record **COPY** must receive:
  - the **combination number** (from CSAV)
  - the **combination type COMB**

These new load cases can then be used in further calculations (e.g., **ASE**).

#### 7) Transformation scope and warnings
The table notes that transformation from saved combinations into loads is only possible for **initial load cases containing “real” loads**. Initial load cases based on **internal forces or derived results** (not real loads) are excluded and trigger warnings in SOFiLOAD.

It also lists superposition results that **cannot be transformed** into loads, including:
- Difference load cases from CSM construction stage
- Internal forces from modal analyses (workflow earthquake)
- Eigenvalue results
- Results from time-step-method calculations

#### 8) Example workflow shown
The example demonstrates:
1. Running two TRAC commands for different resulting load cases (**LC 2155** and **LC 2156**) at **element node** context (node 12) and saving them into **CSAV combination numbers 55 and 56**.
2. Using SOFiLOAD to create **new load cases 201 and 202** via COPY:
   - **LC 201** uses **COMB 55**
   - **LC 202** uses **COMB 56**
3. Computing with ASE using **LC 201, 202**.

Overall, the table captures TRAC’s role as a diagnostic tool for MAXiMA superpositions and explains how traced factor information can be persisted (CSAV), transformed (SOFiLOAD), and reused in subsequent analysis runs (ASE).

The table describes parameters used with the **TRAC** command (see also **SUPP**, **TRAC** context) for investigating how a specified **resulting load case** was generated via a **MAXiMA superposition**. TRAC discovers and prints the **input load cases** that contributed to a chosen resulting load case, including the **factor** used for each input load case. A key capability is that the traced load case factors can be **saved** and later converted into new load cases/loads via **CSAV → SOFiLOAD**.

## Table structure
The table has columns:

- **Item**: Identifier for each parameter group (blank for the first row; explicitly “CSAV” for the second).
- **Description**: Human-readable explanation of the parameter’s function.
- **Unit**: The unit column is present but not used here (both entries show no specific unit).

## Row 1 (Item blank; parameter “F”)
- **Parameter/Item**: **F**
- **Description**: “**Filter out input Load Cases that do not contribute to the superposition**.”
- **Meaning in TRAC terms**: When enabled/used, TRAC omits any input load cases that were part of intermediate consideration but **have zero or no actual contribution** to the computed superposition result for the target. This reduces output size and focuses only on load cases that genuinely influence the traced resulting load case.

## Row 2 (Item: CSAV)
- **Parameter/Item**: **CSAV**
- **Description**: “**Saving of a new combination number (1–999).** The determined load cases with their factors are saved in a new load case combination.”
- **Meaning in TRAC terms**: After TRAC identifies contributing input load cases and their factors, specifying **CSAV** stores this set as a **new combination** with a user-chosen combination number between **1 and 999**. The saved combination can later be used in **SOFiLOAD** to create **new load cases** that replicate the traced superposition factors.

## Practical implications (linked to surrounding documentation)
- The table’s **F** option supports analysis by controlling *which* contributing inputs are reported.
- The **CSAV** option supports workflow automation: the traced combination factors are persisted and can be transformed into new load cases (with **COPY** and **COMB** in SOFiLOAD), then computed in **ASE**.
- However, conversion is limited to load cases derived from “real” loads; internal-force-derived or non-real-load initial cases may produce warnings and may not be transformed.
